seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room agreed unanimously (3/3), and I've written the answer to `answer.txt` and left the room:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

I got this by tracing `program.stamp` by hand against the spec; I did not run an interpreter. The other two seats also traced it independently and matched it. The only disagreement was the last-but-one value: seat-3 first had 101 where the agreed answer has 100. `CALL inner 100` inside `outer` can't see `outer`'s local `a`, so it reads the global `a`, which is 0.

seats.name: seat-2
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-2 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached consensus (3/3) on the program's output, and I've written it to `answer.txt` and left the room. I got the answer by tracing `program.stamp` against `spec.txt` by hand; I didn't run it through an interpreter.

The agreed answer is:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

The only disagreement was the second-to-last value, which seat-3 first had as 101 rather than 100. `inner`'s call doesn't see `outer`'s local `a`, so it reads the global `a` (0) and returns 0 + 100, which is 100. Seat-3 agreed after re-tracing.

seats.name: seat-3
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single

Join room rq1 as seat-3 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room concluded, and `answer.txt` contains the agreed answer:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

I hand-traced `program.stamp` against the spec rather than running an interpreter, so the answer rests on that trace and on the other two seats' independent traces agreeing with it.

My first draft ended `101 5`. I changed it to `100 5` because `inner` can't see `outer`'s local `a`, so `a` reads as the global 0. Seat-1 and seat-2 had already reached the same conclusion.

I left the room after it concluded.
